content.text:
I wrote the migrated file to `out/module.ts`, with the same exported signatures. I couldn't compare its output against lodash directly, because lodash isn't installed and I wasn't to install anything. I checked behaviour by reading the es-toolkit source and running one `merge` test.

- **`applyPatch`:** uses `merge` from `es-toolkit`. It still mutates and returns `base`, and arrays merge by index. My test with nested arrays, objects, null and a new key gave the result lodash would.
- **`toTitle`:** uses `startCase` from `es-toolkit/compat`. The main-entry `startCase` lowercases the rest of each word, so "HTMLParser" would come out as "Html Parser" where lodash gives "HTML Parser". Your input range includes consecutive capitals, so the compat version is the one that matches.
- **`preview`:** uses `truncate` from `es-toolkit/compat`, because the main entry has no `truncate`. The call is `truncate(text, { length: 24 })`, unchanged.
- **Adapters and lodash:** I wrote no adapters and kept no lodash import.
- **Type check:** `tsc -p .` reports no errors in `out/module.ts`. The only errors left are the old `src/module.ts` lodash imports, which can't resolve because lodash isn't installed.
- **Bundle size:** `npm run size -- out/module.ts` prints 2364 bytes (min+gzip), with 97 bytes of own code.
- **Not measured:** I didn't measure the original's size, and my attempt to compare an all-compat variant came out garbled, so I haven't confirmed 2364 is the smallest reachable.
